question: Can weighting ensemble members of a small score-based diffusion model by their training-set score-matching loss lower the Frechet distance of generated samples relative to the arithmetic-mean ensemble?
method: Five-member MLP noise-prediction ensemble, DDIM-style sampler; baseline averages member scores uniformly; improved weights each member by inverse noise-prediction MSE measured on the training set (no pilot sampling, no extra training). Frechet distance in a PCA feature space fitted on training data. Seeds 42, 43, 44.
metric_name: Frechet distance (20-D PCA feature space, lower is better)
baseline: Arithmetic-mean deep-ensemble score model (uniform member weights).
improved: Same members, sampler and seeds; member weights proportional to 1/MSE of each member's noise prediction on the training set; weighted mean of scores.
notes: Test set has 540 digits, so the real reference set uses all of them rather than 1,000. Frechet distance is computed on PCA features, not Inception features, so values are not comparable to FID in the paper. Only three seeds; std is across seeds. The improved weighting uses only training data and adds one forward pass per member (no pilot sampling), so sampling compute is identical to the baseline. Weights are based on in-sample training loss, which may favour members that fit the training set more closely. The weighting rule was fixed a priori (inverse MSE); nothing was tuned or selected on the test set. The classifier and PCA use training data only. Results are from a small toy setting; the reported improvement is whatever the run produced and may be negative.
